method: Read-only source consistency review; git diff confirms reviewed paths equal cb8ce67. No browser, native execution, calculations, tests, or source edits.

findings.title: The v1 walkthrough names a removed button and omits the now-required version choice.
findings.observed: It instructs users to select Already have results? then Try the 17-case HTL pilot. That latter button no longer exists.

evidence.meaning: The combined-project example defaults to v2.
Current UI has Worked HTL example version selector and Load selected example. v1 must be selected to get the 17-case project.

findings.user_impact: Following the public v1 package walkthrough either stalls at a nonexistent control or loads the default 37-case v2 project while expecting the failed 17-case pilot.
findings.minimum_correction: Name the current version selector, explicitly choose v1 / original 17-case pilot, then Load selected example. No evidence data changes.

findings.title: The linked legacy guide says uploads disappear on reload, while the workspace restores them.
findings.observed: The guide states: local uploads disappear on reload.

evidence.meaning: restore reads tab session storage and restores the imported project.
Staged worksheets and applied-sheet flags are also restored.
restore is called on page initialization.
Current docs correctly describe retained applied inputs and staged work in the tab session.
The legacy guide remains directly linked from the current limits page.

findings.user_impact: A reader may treat refresh as a way to clear imported process data or think an undownloaded project has vanished, while the prior data, mappings and drafts are actually restored.
findings.minimum_correction: State that same-tab reload can restore session inputs/drafts; a project download is needed for durable retention. Do not describe reload as clearing data.

consistent_claims.conclusion: Five-table mapped steady-state data, explicit units/topology/product basis, supplied inventory and category factors; no automatic interpretation of arbitrary Aspen reports.

Native .bkp discovery/scans require licensed local Aspen and reviewed controls. Only the published v2 bundle with matching original-byte size/hash enables browser frozen-mean evaluation; uploaded bundles remain inspection/local-CLI inputs.

consistent_claims.topic: v1 failure and one v2 extension
consistent_claims.conclusion: Original failed 335 C / 8.5 m verification is retained. V2 uses one adaptive extension and one fit with original12+new8 training; unchanged 5% policy and floors, no failed point silently removed.

37 unique 20/3/14 cases and 38 retained runs are distinguished; fresh4 are reported separately from legacy holdout3, legacy verification2 and local8. Known development groups are not called fresh independent tests.

Inventory characterization requires supplied factors, missing categories remain incomplete, no background database/ISO or physical validation claim. Generic energy/impact use kg outlet target; old HTL electricity uses 100kg wet feed/1h and climate remains kg target. Heater/reactor efficiency1, fixedpump and separator/cooling exclusions are disclosed.

External steady-state models require reviewed node/unit/range/topology/product/LCA mappings and local model-specific testing; no claim of arbitrary unreviewed .bkp automatic LCA or browser native simulation.

not_a_finding: Production /README.md 404 is a non-runtime documentation route as instructed; no deployment change requested.
The model viewer says declared model digests are not independently recomputed. This is compatible with the separate file-byte SHA256 check used only to enable the public v2 query.
Historical README sections explicitly identify their stage; old stage-specific statements were not treated as current claims.
limits: Source review establishes wording consistency, not new scientific validation. HTTP and browser behavior are covered by separate acceptance records.
